From 82a5cc783d49b86afd2f60e297ecd85223c39f88 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Konstantin Taranov <kotaranov@microsoft.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Jun 2024 01:16:08 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] RDMA/mana_ib: Ignore optional access flags for MRs

Ignore optional ib_access_flags when an MR is created.

Fixes: 0266a177631d ("RDMA/mana_ib: Add a driver for Microsoft Azure Network Adapter")
Signed-off-by: Konstantin Taranov <kotaranov@microsoft.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/1717575368-14879-1-git-send-email-kotaranov@linux.microsoft.com
Signed-off-by: Leon Romanovsky <leon@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/infiniband/hw/mana/mr.c b/drivers/infiniband/hw/mana/mr.c
index 4f13423ecdbd..887b09dd86e7 100644
--- a/drivers/infiniband/hw/mana/mr.c
+++ b/drivers/infiniband/hw/mana/mr.c
@@ -112,6 +112,7 @@ struct ib_mr *mana_ib_reg_user_mr(struct ib_pd *ibpd, u64 start, u64 length,
 		  "start 0x%llx, iova 0x%llx length 0x%llx access_flags 0x%x",
 		  start, iova, length, access_flags);
 
+	access_flags &= ~IB_ACCESS_OPTIONAL;
 	if (access_flags & ~VALID_MR_FLAGS)
 		return ERR_PTR(-EINVAL);
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/infiniband/hw/mana/mr.c`**
   - A new line was added to modify the `access_flags` variable by masking out the optional access flags. Specifically, the line `access_flags &= ~IB_ACCESS_OPTIONAL;` was introduced before the validation of the `access_flags`. This change ensures that any optional access flags are ignored when creating a memory region (MR).

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `mr.c` directly addresses a bug related to the handling of optional access flags during the creation of memory regions in the RDMA/mana_ib driver. By ignoring these optional flags, the patch resolves potential issues that may arise from their inclusion, thereby improving the robustness of the driver. This change is linked to a previous commit (identified by the hash `0266a177631d`) that introduced the driver, indicating that the current fix is a corrective measure for a flaw introduced in that earlier implementation.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
access_flags,
if (access_flags & ~VALID_MR_FLAGS)
```
Reason:
The `access_flags` variable includes optional access flags that may not be relevant for the memory region (MR) being created. If these optional flags are not properly handled, they can lead to invalid configurations, causing errors when checking against `VALID_MR_FLAGS`.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
access_flags &= ~IB_ACCESS_OPTIONAL;
if (access_flags & ~VALID_MR_FLAGS)
```
Reason:
The patch masks out the optional access flags from `access_flags` before performing any validation. This ensures that only valid access flags are considered during MR creation, preventing potential errors or invalid configurations.
